title: AN ORDINANCE CLOSING OFF THE CITY OF DAVAO TO MINING OPERATIONS

sections.heading: TITLE
sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known and cited as 'An Ordinance Closing Off the City of Davao to Mining Operations' or the 'Davao City Mining Closure Ordinance of 2015'.

sections.heading: DECLARATION OF POLICY
sections.text: It is hereby declared the policy of the City Government of Davao to maintain ecological balance, safeguard its potable water sources, preserve agricultural landholdings, and shield its inhabitants from the devastating effects of extractive mineral exploration and exploitation.

sections.heading: TERRITORIAL COVERAGE
sections.text: The provisions of this Ordinance shall strictly apply to all lands, upland territories, ancestral domains, watershed recharge areas, conservation zones, and water bodies located within the entire territorial jurisdiction of Davao City.

sections.heading: DEFINITION OF TERMS
sections.text:
For purposes of this Ordinance, the following terms shall be defined as follows:

a. Mining — refers to the extraction, exploration, prospecting, utilization, development, or processing of minerals, whether metallic or non-metallic, through open-pit, underground, tunneling, placer, or chemical leaching mechanisms.

b. Metallic Minerals — refer to minerals such as gold, copper, nickel, chromite, iron, silver, and other base or precious metallic ores.

c. Quarry Resources — refer to common rocks, sand, gravel, earthfill, diorite, limestone, and other non-metallic minerals used exclusively for building and infrastructure construction that do not contain valuable metallic ores in economically workable quantities.

d. Mineral Agreements — refer to national contracts, permits, Financial or Technical Assistance Agreements (FTAAs), or Mineral Production Sharing Agreements (MPSAs) granted under Republic Act No. 7942.

sections.heading: PROHIBITION ON MINING OPERATIONS
sections.text: No approval, clearance, permit, or endorsement shall be granted or issued by the City of Davao through its Sangguniang Panlungsod or the City Mayor to any person, natural or juridical, to undertake any and all forms of mining operation, mineral exploration, prospecting, or processing in any area within the territorial jurisdiction of Davao City. The City Mayor and all administrative departments are expressly prohibited from issuing Mayor's Clearances, Business Permits, or Locational Approvals to mining concessionaires holding national mineral agreements.

sections.heading: EXEMPTION OF TRADITIONAL QUARRY RESOURCES
sections.text: The prohibition established under Section 5 shall not apply to the extraction of non-metallic quarry resources, such as sand, gravel, boulder, and earthfill for local construction needs; Provided, that said extraction strictly adheres to the Davao City Watershed Code, possesses valid environmental compliance certificates, does not involve metallic substances, and secures prior written clearance from the City Mining Regulatory Board.

sections.heading: PENAL SANCTIONS
sections.text:
Any person or corporate entity that violates the provisions of this Ordinance shall be punished by a fine of Five Thousand Pesos (₱5,000.00) and imprisonment of not less than six (6) months nor more than one (1) year, or both, at the discretion of the court.

In addition, the business permit of the offending entity shall be perpetually cancelled, its mining machinery and extractive equipment impounded and forfeited in favor of the City Government, and its operational site subject to summary physical closure.

sections.heading: SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
sections.text: If, for any reason, any section or provision of this Ordinance is held unconstitutional or invalid by a competent court, the other sections or provisions not affected thereby shall remain in full force and effect.

sections.heading: EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect immediately upon its approval and publication in a local newspaper of general circulation in Davao City.
